exposure: Biologic DMARDs (bDMARDs) exposure (preconceptionally or during pregnancy)
cohort: 244 pregnancies were studied, including 128 women with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases or inflammatory bowel disease) and 116 healthy pregnant women as a comparison group.
finding: The use of bDMARDs in pregnant women with IMIDs was effective in disease control and safe from a maternal-fetal perspective, showing no increased risk of prematurity, SGA, malformations, or infections.
mod_finding: Cesarean sections were more frequently performed in gestations where the mother was treated with bDMARDs, particularly anti-TNF agents.
